newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares continue firm in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares continue firm in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks continued firm in brisk trade on Thursday, benefitting from investors deserting the local money market where interest rates were low and unattractive.
"The (stock) market is still very strong and still being driven by low interest rates on the money market," one broker said.
"We still have to see what will happen after the government stock issue which closed today," he said.

The government came into the money market last week to float a seven-year issue which market sources said looked set to siphon over Z$1 billion from the system. Some dealers therefore expected rates to firm.

On Thursday, the key 57-counter industrial stock index surged 130.93 points to a record 8,648.33, largely on the back of a 300 cent gain in tobacco group Rothmans to 4,500, banking group FMB which put on 150 cents to 4,250, and 100 cent advances in conglomerate Delta and clothing retailer Edgars, which traded at 3,800 and 3,700 respectively.

Other gains were in electronics group Apex and cool drink company Schweppes, both 15 cents stronger at 175 and 365 respectively, while investors IHL, cement group Porthold and tobacco concern TSL all added 20 cents to 1,850, 1,500 and 700.
Wine maker Cairns put on 25 cents to 1,325, Mashonaland Holdings went up 30 cents to 280 banking group Barclays were 40 cents firmer at 2,400 and Circem gained 50 cents to 850.

In minings, gold miners Rio Tinto added 300 cents to 2,900 and the seven-share index went up 7.18 points to 1,042.20. undeterred by a 40 cent loss in nickel producer Bindura to 760 and gold giant Ashanti which shed 500 cents to 11,000. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 2/8/9--
